grades.question: How is rule determined, including ordinary ties, Eyrie ties, tokens and the Vagabond pawn?
grades.expected_answer: More total warriors plus buildings than each other player; ordinary ties mean no ruler. Eyrie win a tie for most if they have at least one Eyrie piece there. Tokens and pawns do not contribute; Vagabond cannot rule or prevent rule.

observed.answer: Rule is determined by comparing each player's total warriors plus buildings in a clearing. Tokens and pawns do not count. grades.question: What makes a normal move legal, can the same warriors move repeatedly, and do rivers count as paths?
grades.expected_answer: Move more than zero warriors/pawns along one linking path to an adjacent clearing; rule origin or destination or both. Same pieces can move repeatedly. Rivers are not paths unless explicitly treated as such.

observed.answer: A normal move takes any positive number of your warriors or pawns from one clearing along a linking path to an adjacent clearing. You must rule the origin, destination, or both, and recheck rule for each move. The same pieces may move repeatedly, including across multiple moves in one action. Rivers are not paths unless an effect explicitly says otherwise.

grades.question: Describe battle from ambush through removal: foiling, early ending, dice limits, extra hits, removal priorities and who scores removed buildings/tokens.
grades.expected_answer: Defender may ambush matching clearing; attacker may foil with matching ambush. Unfoiled ambush deals two immediate hits; discard defender ambush, end battle if no attacking warriors/pawns remain. Before-roll effects, roll high attacker/low defender, rolled hits capped by own warriors, after-roll effects, count hits including uncapped extra hits and defenseless extra attacker hit if no defending warriors, then deal hits. Each side chooses own removals, warriors first. Whoever removes enemy building/token scores one, including defender.

observed.answer: The defender may play one matching Ambush (birds are wild); the attacker may foil it with a matching Ambush. A foiled Ambush deals no hits; otherwise the defender immediately deals two hits, not limited by defending warriors, and the battle ends immediately if no attacking warriors or pawns remain. Resolve before-roll effects, roll dice (higher result is attacker's hits and lower is defender's; ties give equal results), then after-roll effects. Each side's rolled hits are capped by its own warriors in battle, with Alliance defending reversing the dice and Vagabond using undamaged swords instead of warriors. Add extra hits without a warrior cap, subtract ignored hits, and give the attacker one defenseless hit if defender has no warriors (for Vagabond, no undamaged swords). Each hit removes one opposing piece. The taking side chooses its removal order, but must remove all its warriors before buildings or tokens; it also orders its removal-trigger effects. Both sides deal counted hits even if warriors were removed during the exchange. Whoever removes an enemy building or token scores one VP each, including a defender and outside battle. Vagabond takes hits as item damage.
observed.evidence: Actions → Battle (4.3), six numbered steps, especially Ambush, Roll, Count hits, and Deal hits.

grades.question: How does the Eyrie resolve its Decree, including action suit locations, within-column order and Build restrictions?
grades.expected_answer: Craft first; resolve all cards Recruit,Move,Battle,Build in that column order, cards in any order within column. Recruit at matching roost; Move from matching clearing with at least one warrior; Battle in matching clearing; Build in matching ruled clearing without roost and open slot. Bird wild. Inability fully resolve immediately causes turmoil.

observed.answer: Craft with roosts first, then resolve every Decree card by columns in Recruit, Move, Battle, Build order; within a column, choose the card order freely. Bird is wild. Recruit places a warrior at a roost in a clearing matching the card (two with Charismatic); Move must move at least one warrior from a matching clearing and obey normal movement restrictions; Battle must begin in a matching clearing with your warriors and an enemy; Build places a roost in a matching clearing you rule with an open slot and no existing roost. A Decree Build cannot be completed if any of those restrictions fail; inability to complete any required Decree action causes Turmoil.

grades.question: What exactly happens in Turmoil, including Viziers, leaders, pieces on map and the rest of the turn?

observed.answer: In Turmoil, lose one VP per bird Decree card, including both Loyal Viziers. grades.question: When does Outrage trigger, what is paid, and what if the player has no matching card or the supporter stack is full?
grades.expected_answer: Another player removing sympathy or moving any warriors into sympathetic clearing owes one matching hand card including bird to supporters. Merely battling without removing sympathy is not trigger. If none matching show hand to Alliance; Alliance draws deck card to supporters. No bases caps stack at five; incoming overflow discarded.

observed.answer: Outrage triggers when another player removes sympathy or moves any warriors into a sympathetic clearing. The player adds one matching hand card, with birds counting as a match, to Supporters; moving a group costs one card per affected move, not per warrior. If they have no matching card including birds, they show their hand to the Alliance, which draws one card from the deck into Supporters. With no base, the stack holds at most five supporters and incoming excess cards are discarded; with a base, capacity is unlimited.

grades.question: How do Alliance Revolt and Spread Sympathy differ in timing/order, eligible clearing, supporter cost, martial law and results?
grades.expected_answer: Birdsong Revolt before Spread, each any number. Revolt: sympathetic clearing without base whose matching base is on board, pay two matching supporters, remove all enemy pieces, place matching base, warriors equal matching sympathetic clearings, one officer, score removed enemy buildings/tokens. Spread: unsympathetic adjacent to sympathy or any clearing if none; pay shown matching supporters plus one if at least three warriors of one other player; place sympathy and score uncovered points.

observed.answer: In Birdsong, the Alliance may Revolt any number of times first, then Spread Sympathy any number of times. Revolt chooses a sympathetic clearing without a base matching a base still on the board, spends two matching supporters, removes all enemy pieces there, places that base, places warriors equal to matching-suit sympathy clearings (including the revolt clearing), and places one warrior in Officers; it scores normal VP for enemy buildings/tokens removed and needs a legal base slot. Spread Sympathy chooses an unsympathetic clearing adjacent by path to existing sympathy, or any clearing if none exists; it spends the supporter cost shown above the next sympathy token, plus one matching supporter under Martial Law when one other player has at least three warriors there. It places sympathy and scores the uncovered space. Only one sympathy may occupy a clearing; the Keep's placement ban applies.
observed.evidence: Woodland Alliance (8) — Birdsong: Revolt and Spread Sympathy.

observed.answer: Train during Daylight by spending a hand card matching a clearing with a base to place one supply warrior in Officers; Supporters cannot pay for Train. When a base is removed, discard supporters matching its clearing, including birds, remove half the officers rounded up, and if no bases remain discard supporters down to five.

grades.question: How do Vagabond refresh, Slip, normal Move and forest Rest work, including hostile destinations and Evening drawing?
grades.expected_answer: Refresh two exhausted items per tea already face up on track, then three more; newly refreshed tea does not boost that step. Slip optionally adjacent clearing/forest free boots even hostile, ignoring restrictions on moving out. Normal Move costs boot plus extra boot if hostile warriors at destination; cannot enter forest, may leave to adjacent clearing, rule ignored. Forest Rest repairs all damaged items and flips them face up; still draw one plus face-up coins on track then discard to five.

observed.answer: In Birdsong, refresh two exhausted items per tea already face up on the Refresh track, then three more; tea refreshed during this step does not add refreshes that step. Optional Slip moves to an adjacent clearing or forest without exhausting boots and can enter hostile warriors, ignoring effects that prevent movement out of a clearing. A normal Daylight move exhausts one boot plus one extra boot if the destination has warriors of any Hostile faction; it ignores rule, cannot enter a forest, and from a forest can move only to an adjacent clearing. In a forest during Evening, Rest returns all damaged items to Satchel face up and moves ready tea/coins/bags to tracks if possible, but does not refresh undamaged exhausted items. Vagabond always draws one card plus one per face-up coin on track, even after Rest.
observed.evidence: Vagabond (9; V.1–3) — Birdsong, Daylight Move, and Evening.

grades.question: When does a faction become Hostile to Vagabond, when is Infamy scored, can Aid undo Hostility, and what does Strike target?
grades.expected_answer: Removing any one non-hostile faction warrior makes Hostile. Infamy one extra VP per hostile piece removed in battle during own turn except warrior causing hostility; no Infamy for Strike. Aid cannot undo hostility but can take crafted item. Strike exhaust crossbow, removes enemy warrior, or other faction piece if that enemy has no warriors there.

observed.answer: Removing one warrior of a non-Hostile faction immediately makes it Hostile, except allied warriors removed during a battle against that same faction: if more allied warriors are removed than items damaged, it becomes Hostile at battle end; equal numbers do not trigger this. On your own turn during battle, score one extra VP per hostile piece removed, except the warrior that first made that faction Hostile; add ordinary building/token removal points. There is no Infamy while defending on another player's turn or from Strike. Aid cannot undo Hostility, though it can still take a crafted item. Strike exhausts a crossbow to remove one enemy warrior; only if that enemy has no warriors in the clearing may you remove another piece of that faction. Strike is not battle and gives no Infamy.
observed.evidence: Vagabond (9; V.1–3) — Strike; Relationships: Hostile and Infamy; Aid.

grades.question: What are coalition eligibility, timing, VP requirement, partner selection and victory, and what changes if partner is Hostile?
grades.expected_answer: Vagabond cannot use normal dominance win. With four or more players during own Daylight at least 10 VP activates dominance to coalition with lowest VP other player not already in coalition, choose tied lowest. Place score marker on partner board, stop scoring; partner win means Vagabond also wins. Hostile partner relationship becomes Indifferent.

observed.answer: With four or more players, in its own Daylight at 10 or more VP, Vagabond may activate dominance to form a coalition with a player not already in a coalition. The partner must have the lowest VP among players other than Vagabond; Vagabond chooses among ties. Vagabond puts its score marker on the partner's faction board and stops scoring. If the partner wins, including by dominance, Vagabond also wins. A Hostile partner becomes Indifferent; coalition alone does not grant Allied relationship powers.
